head: pr17394-r8
report:
I’ll trace the lease and cleanup paths, then probe failure and cross-process races against the production functions. All fixtures will stay in scratch.


Three claims need probing: lease failures preserve safety; the last lease releases deferred teardown across processes; and lease acquisition cannot race deletion. The code swallows lease-directory and lease-write errors, stores deferred teardown only in process memory, and creates leases without the cleanup lock.


The probes reproduced deletion of a live borrower’s workspace after a lease-directory read fault, a swallowed lease-write failure, a symlink-based open, and a lease arriving after cleanup’s scan. A second process’s final release—and its `SIGKILL`—left deferred capture unrun. Separately, a delayed native stop deleted successor data after the ten-second lock timeout.


## P1 — Keep the sandbox locked until an in-place backend stop has actually finished

**File:** `packages/coding-agent/src/task/worktree.ts:840–843,872`

**Mechanism:** When retirement rename fails, `cleanupIsolation()` starts an in-place `isoStop()`. After ten seconds it releases the sandbox lock without cancelling that stop. A successor can acquire the lock and write a new generation, but the old stop still targets the successor’s directory. The generation check does not protect this late deletion.

**Trigger:** Inject `EBUSY` into the retirement rename, delay the backend stop past ten seconds, acquire the released lock and create successor data, then allow the original native `isoStop()` to execute. The probe delays the real native function; it does not substitute a deletion implementation.

**Command run** from the snapshot’s `packages/coding-agent` directory:
```sh
bun test /mnt/nvme/sami/tmp/cachefix/reviewer-evals/runs/scratch/crossfamily__pr17394-r8__t2/late-stop.test.ts
```

**Measured output:**
```text
{"cleanupElapsedMs":10021,"stopStillBlocked":true}
{"successorCreatedUnderLock":true,"successorSurvivedLateNativeStop":false,"successorClaimIntact":true}
```

The successor’s owner marker survived while its data was deleted. Timeout must not make the pathname reusable while destructive work against it remains outstanding.

## P1 — Serialize lease acquisition with cleanup’s check and deletion

**Files:** `packages/coding-agent/src/task/isolation-lease.ts:119–125`; `packages/coding-agent/src/task/worktree.ts:808–811`

**Mechanism:** Cleanup holds the sandbox lock while checking leases, but `leaseIsolationWorkspace()` never acquires that lock. A borrower can successfully publish a lease after the empty scan and before retirement rename. Cleanup then moves and deletes the workspace, including the newly published lease.

**Trigger:** Pause production `cleanupIsolation()` immediately before its retirement rename. Start a second Bun process that calls production `leaseIsolationWorkspace()`, wait for its successful acquisition, then resume the rename.

**Command run:**
```sh
bun test /mnt/nvme/sami/tmp/cachefix/reviewer-evals/runs/scratch/crossfamily__pr17394-r8__t2/cross-process.test.ts
```

**Measured output:**
```text
{"scenario":"cross-process lease before rename","liveAtRename":true,"workExists":false}
```

The lock protects materialization and cleanup from each other, but not the new borrower path. Lease publication needs the same synchronization and a check that the sandbox is still available.

## P1 — Preserve the workspace when its lease directory cannot be read

**File:** `packages/coding-agent/src/task/isolation-lease.ts:93`

**Mechanism:** `fs.readdir(leaseDir).catch(() => [])` converts every enumeration failure into “no leases.” `deferTeardownWhileLeased()` consequently authorizes cleanup even when a live borrower’s lease exists.

**Trigger:** Create a sandbox and a live lease, inject an error only into enumeration of `.omp-isolation-leases`, then call production `cleanupIsolation()`. The probe exercised `EIO`, `ENOSPC`, `EACCES`, `EXDEV`, `EBUSY`, and `ENOTEMPTY`; every case deleted the workspace.

**Command run:**
```sh
bun test /mnt/nvme/sami/tmp/cachefix/reviewer-evals/runs/scratch/crossfamily__pr17394-r8__t2/lease-faults.test.ts
```

**Measured output, excerpts:**
```text
{"operation":"readdir","code":"EIO","liveBefore":true,"cleanupReturned":true,"workExists":false}
{"operation":"readdir","code":"EACCES","liveBefore":true,"cleanupReturned":true,"workExists":false}
{"operation":"readdir","code":"EBUSY","liveBefore":true,"cleanupReturned":true,"workExists":false}
```

Only an absent lease directory can safely mean an empty inventory. Other read failures must block reclamation or propagate.

## P1 — Reject an opening session when its lease cannot be persisted

**File:** `packages/coding-agent/src/task/isolation-lease.ts:124–128`

**Mechanism:** Lease persistence failure is logged at debug level and replaced with a successful no-op release function. Both `sdk.ts:4478` and `structured-subagent.ts:880` then proceed without protection. The owner can delete the workspace under that session.

**Trigger:** Inject failure into the atomic rename that publishes the lease, await `leaseIsolationWorkspace()`, then invoke the owner’s cleanup. The probe exercised all six error codes listed above.

**Command run:**
```sh
bun test /mnt/nvme/sami/tmp/cachefix/reviewer-evals/runs/scratch/crossfamily__pr17394-r8__t2/lease-faults.test.ts
```

**Measured output, excerpts:**
```text
{"operation":"lease rename","code":"EIO","leaseReturned":true,"live":false,"workExists":false}
{"operation":"lease rename","code":"ENOSPC","leaseReturned":true,"live":false,"workExists":false}
{"operation":"lease rename","code":"EACCES","leaseReturned":true,"live":false,"workExists":false}
```

“No sandbox exists” and “the required lease could not be recorded” must not return the same successful result.

## P1 — Resolve cwd aliases before discovering the sandbox to lease

**File:** `packages/coding-agent/src/task/isolation-lease.ts:59–63,72–79`

**Mechanism:** Both local ownership lookup and on-disk discovery use `path.resolve()`, not filesystem canonicalization. A symlink pointing directly to the merged directory neither matches the registered canonical path nor exposes an ancestor named `m` or `merged`. Lease acquisition silently returns a no-op.

This is reachable through the SDK: `options.cwd` is accepted without canonicalization, and the lease is taken against `sessionManager.getCwd()`.

**Trigger:** Create a real symlink named `sandbox-alias` pointing to a registered sandbox’s `m` directory. Acquire a lease using that alias, then clean up the owner.

**Command run:**
```sh
bun test /mnt/nvme/sami/tmp/cachefix/reviewer-evals/runs/scratch/crossfamily__pr17394-r8__t2/lease-faults.test.ts
```

**Measured output:**
```text
{"operation":"symlink lease","live":false,"workExists":false}
```

No fault injection was used for this case. The real filesystem alias bypassed lease protection.

## P1 — Wake the owning process when the last remote lease ends

**File:** `packages/coding-agent/src/task/isolation-lease.ts:135–142,153–162`

**Mechanism:** Lease records are persistent, but `pendingTeardown` exists only in the owner’s process-local map. A remote borrower’s release removes its file and returns at line 135 because it has no locally registered workspace. Nothing notifies or polls in the owning process. `SIGKILL` likewise leaves no event that runs the pending callback.

`runIsolatedSubprocess()` defers its entire `captureAndCleanup` callback through this mechanism at `isolation-runner.ts:481`, so this strands final capture as well as cleanup.

**Trigger:** Have process A register the sandbox. Process B acquires its lease and signals readiness. A calls production `deferTeardownWhileLeased()` with a callback that counts invocation and performs cleanup. Let B write its final edit and either release normally or receive `SIGKILL`. After B exits, query lease liveness and reclamation from A.

**Command run:**
```sh
bun test /mnt/nvme/sami/tmp/cachefix/reviewer-evals/runs/scratch/crossfamily__pr17394-r8__t2/cross-process.test.ts
```

**Measured output:**
```text
child: released
{"mode":"release","deferred":true,"liveAfter":false,"captures":0,"workExists":true,"reclaimable":false,"reason":"a live task owns it"}
child: waiting-for-kill
{"mode":"kill","deferred":true,"liveAfter":false,"captures":0,"workExists":true,"reclaimable":false,"reason":"a live task owns it"}
```

Even an explicit liveness scan after the borrower exited did not discharge the deferred work. Ordinary reclamation also refused the workspace because the owning host remained alive. The owner needs a cross-process completion mechanism that also handles crashed borrowers.

**Verdict: Not safe to merge.**
